email.test.subject: Mail Concierge test e-mail
email.test.body:
Hello,

This is a test e-mail sent by Mail Concierge. If you are reading it, e-mail sending works.

cfg.title: Mail Concierge
cfg.templatesLang: Templates shown: {0}. Templates of other languages are kept as they are.
cfg.enabledHint: Available once the public URL, the SMTP server and the sender address are saved.
cfg.native: Do not use Mail Concierge for “Forgot password”
cfg.nativeHint: Jellyfin then keeps its own behaviour: it writes a PIN to a file on the server, and only for requests from the local network. No e-mail is sent.
cfg.publicUrlHint: Every link in e-mails is built from it (for example https://jellyfin.example.org). Nothing is sent while it is empty.
cfg.defaultLanguageHint: Used for e-mails sent to users who have not chosen a language.
cfg.logoEmbeddedHint: The logo is attached to the message: it shows without a click and without asking your server for anything (about 30 KB more per e-mail).
cfg.logoHostedHint: The logo is loaded from your public address when the message is opened: lighter e-mails, but some mail apps block the image and your server sees the opening.
cfg.allowAdminsHint: Off by default: administrators can neither reset their password by e-mail nor sign in with their e-mail address.
cfg.sessions: Sessions closed after a password reset
cfg.sessInactive: Only sessions inactive for some days
cfg.secretHint: Write-only. Leave empty to keep the stored value.
cfg.smtpDomainNote: Check the sender's domain with this provider (SPF, DKIM), otherwise messages may end up in spam.
cfg.smtpRetypePassword: Type the password again for this provider.
cfg.publicUrlSuggested: Taken from the address published in Jellyfin: check it, then save.
cfg.smtpPreset.gmail.password: An app password (2-step verification is required), not your usual password.
cfg.smtpPreset.brevo.user: The login shown in Brevo under SMTP & API, SMTP.
cfg.smtpPreset.brevo.password: An SMTP key (not an API key).
cfg.smtpPreset.smtp2go.user: The SMTP user created under Sending, SMTP Users.
cfg.smtpPreset.smtp2go.note: If port 587 is blocked, try port 2525.
cfg.smtpPreset.mailgun.user: The SMTP credential of your sending domain, usually postmaster@your-domain.
cfg.smtpPreset.mailgun.note: Accounts in the US region use smtp.mailgun.org instead of the host above.
cfg.testHint: Save the settings first: the test uses the saved settings.
cfg.err.test_send_failed: the e-mail could not be sent. Check the SMTP host, port, security and credentials; the technical detail is in the Jellyfin log.
cfg.err.test_not_configured: save a valid public URL, SMTP host and sender address first.
cfg.warnSmtpNone: Security “None”: e-mails and the SMTP password travel unencrypted. Use it only on a trusted local network.
cfg.warnHttpPublicUrl: This URL starts with http://: the links in e-mails (recovery, invitations) will travel unencrypted. Use https:// unless this is a private network.
cfg.warnHttpSeerr: This URL starts with http://: the Seerr API key will travel unencrypted. Use https:// unless Seerr is on a trusted local network.
cfg.cancelHours: Validity of the “cancel e-mail change” link (hours)
cfg.maxIp: Forgot-password requests per address per 15 minutes
cfg.maxPin: Wrong PIN attempts before the PIN is cancelled
cfg.adminNotificationAddress: Address to warn when a limit is reached
cfg.quotaLine: {0} of {1} e-mails counted. One recipient can receive up to {2}.
cfg.quotaReached: A daily e-mail limit was reached on {0}: some e-mails were not sent. If this is not expected, check the Jellyfin log, or raise the limits below.
cfg.templatesHint: Edit a template to override it. Placeholders look like {{username}} or {{link}}; keep the ones already in the template. In a .txt template the first line is “Subject: …”.
cfg.seerrEnabled: Keep Seerr e-mail addresses in sync
cfg.importChanged: {0} address(es) changed in Seerr since the preview and were not imported. Open the preview again.
cfg.importWarning: Imported addresses are stored as confirmed without a confirmation e-mail. Import only the addresses you know.
cfg.assignHint: Gives Mail Concierge as password-reset provider to every eligible account (default authentication provider; administrators only if enabled in the General tab).
cfg.assigned: {0} assigned, {1} administrator(s) skipped, {2} external account(s) skipped.
cfg.statsNone: No e-mail sent since the start
cfg.proxyUnknown: Mail Concierge is disabled: a reverse proxy that Jellyfin does not know about was detected (requests come from a private address with an X-Forwarded-For header). Set Known Proxies in Dashboard > Networking. This notice clears by itself after 15 minutes without such a request.
cfg.mailOff: E-mails cannot be sent yet: the public URL, the SMTP server and the sender address must be filled in and valid.
cfg.disabledBanner: Mail Concierge is turned off: tick “Enable Mail Concierge” on the General tab, then save. Until then invitations and e-mail recovery do not work.
cfg.err.invalid_smtp_port: The SMTP port must be between 1 and 65535.
cfg.err.invalid_number: Durations and limits must be positive numbers.
cfg.err.invalid_public_url: The public URL must be an http:// or https:// address, or empty.
cfg.err.invalid_seerr_url: The Seerr URL must be an http:// or https:// address, or empty.
cfg.err.smtp_server_changed: The SMTP server changed: type the password again, or clear it.
cfg.err.seerr_address_changed: The Seerr address changed: type the API key again.
cfg.err.smtp_encryption_off: SMTP encryption was turned off: type the password again, or clear it.
cfg.err.invalid_smtp_security: The SMTP security is not valid.
cfg.err.invalid_sessions: The sessions policy is not valid.
cfg.err.invalid_email_logo: The e-mail logo choice is not valid.
cfg.err.invalid_from_address: The sender address is not valid.
cfg.err.invalid_admin_address: The address to warn is not valid.
cfg.err.invalid_smtp_host: Enter only the server name, for example smtp.example.org, not a web address or a port.
cfg.err.smtp_incomplete: To enable Mail Concierge, the public URL (General tab), the SMTP server and the sender address (SMTP tab) must be saved and valid first. Save them, then tick “Enable” again.
cfg.err.invalid_template: A template is not valid or too large.
cfg.err.invalidEmail: This e-mail address is not valid.
inv.title: Invitations
inv.emailHint: If you type an address, the invitation is sent to it. Otherwise you get a link to copy.
inv.liveTvHint: If left unticked, the invited account cannot watch Live TV. It only appears if your server has Live TV.
inv.copyManual: Select the link above and copy it.
inv.sentTo: The invitation was sent to {0}. The link, if you want to give it yourself:
inv.notSent: The invitation was created but the e-mail could not be sent. Give this link yourself:
inv.notSentLimit: The invitation was created but the e-mail was not sent: the hourly limit for invitation e-mails is reached (see the Limits section of the settings). Give this link yourself:
inv.notSentQueueFull: The e-mail was not sent: the sending queue is full. Check the SMTP server, then send the link yourself or regenerate it later.
inv.linkReady: Invitation created. This link is shown only now:
inv.historyHint: Revoke: the link stops working and the line stays in the history. Erase: the line disappears from the history. A dash in the Access column means the Live TV right is unknown (invitation created before version 12.4.1.0).
inv.errUsername: This user name is not valid.
inv.errEmail: This e-mail address is not valid.
inv.errPublicUrl: The public URL is not set in the Mail Concierge settings, so no link can be made.
inv.errServiceClosed: Mail Concierge is disabled (General tab, “Enable Mail Concierge” box) or blocked by the proxy notice: an invitation cannot be created or sent.
inv.confirmNoLibrary: No library is selected: the new account will see no content until you give it access. Send the invitation anyway?
inv.confirmErasePending: Erase this invitation? Its link will stop working.
inv.confirmErase: Erase this line from the history? This cannot be undone.
inv.newLink: New link created. It is shown only now:
inv.newLinkNotSentLimit: New link created, but the e-mail was not sent: the hourly limit for invitation e-mails is reached (see the Limits section of the settings). Give this link yourself:
cfg.err.invalid_template_subject: The first line of a .txt template must start with “Subject: ”.
cfg.err.seerr_disabled: Seerr is not enabled. Enable it and save the settings first.
cfg.err.seerr_unreachable: Seerr cannot be reached. Check its URL and API key in the saved settings.
cfg.help.publicUrl: The web address of your Jellyfin server as your family sees it (for example https://jellyfin.example.org), used to build the links in e-mails.
cfg.help.defaultLanguage: The language of e-mails sent to users who have not chosen a language.
cfg.help.emailLogo: Chooses how the logo reaches the e-mails sent by Mail Concierge: attached to the message, loaded from your server when the message is opened, or left out.
cfg.help.allowAdministrators: When ticked, administrator accounts can also reset their password by e-mail and sign in with their e-mail address; leave it off to keep administrators out of both.
cfg.help.sessionsOnReset: Chooses which devices are signed out when someone resets their password: all of them, only the ones inactive for the threshold below, or none.
cfg.help.sessionDays: Number of days without activity after which a device counts as inactive; only used when the option above is the inactivity one.
cfg.help.smtpSecurity: How the connection to the mail server is protected; use the option your mail provider gives you (usually STARTTLS on port 587 or SSL/TLS on port 465).
cfg.help.smtpProvider: Choose your provider to fill in the server, the port and the security; with Custom, enter the values your provider gave you.
cfg.help.fromAddress: The e-mail address shown as the sender of the messages Mail Concierge sends; it must be allowed by your mail server.
cfg.help.invitationDays: How long an invitation link stays valid, in days, before it expires.
cfg.help.pinMinutes: How long a recovery PIN code stays valid, in minutes, before a new one is needed.
cfg.help.confirmationHours: How long the link to confirm a new e-mail address stays valid, in hours.
cfg.help.cancelHours: How long the link that lets someone cancel an e-mail address change stays valid, in hours (24 by default). Cancelling also needs the account password.
cfg.help.maxIp: The maximum number of forgot-password requests from one internet address in 15 minutes.
cfg.help.maxPin: The number of wrong PIN attempts allowed (a count, not a time) before that PIN is cancelled and a new one must be requested.
cfg.help.maxEmailsPerRecipient: The maximum number of e-mails of any kind (invitation, password recovery, address confirmation) one recipient can receive in 24 hours. The count rolls: an e-mail leaves it 24 hours after it was sent. The test e-mail and the security notices about an address change are never counted.
cfg.help.maxEmailsPerDay: The maximum number of e-mails Mail Concierge sends in 24 hours, all recipients together. Once it is reached, no more e-mails are sent until older ones leave the 24-hour count. The test e-mail and the security notices about an address change are never counted.
cfg.help.adminNotificationAddress: Optional. Mail Concierge sends an e-mail to this address when a daily limit is reached, at most once a day for each limit. It only contains counts, never the address of a recipient. Leave empty to receive no e-mail: the warning stays in the Jellyfin log and on this page.
cfg.help.templates: The wording of the e-mails Mail Concierge sends: change a template to personalise it, or leave it empty to keep the built-in text.
cfg.help.seerrUrl: The web address of your Seerr server (for example http://seerr:5055), used to match Jellyfin accounts with Seerr users.
cfg.help.seerrApiKey: The secret key found in Seerr under Settings, General, which lets Mail Concierge talk to Seerr; it is stored securely and never shown again.
cfg.help.assignProvider: Makes Mail Concierge the password-reset method of every eligible account in one click, so the e-mail reset works for everybody.
cfg.emailLogin: Allow sign-in with the e-mail address
cfg.emailLoginShared: {0} confirmed address(es) are shared by several accounts and cannot be used to sign in.
cfg.emailLoginUnavailable: Not available with this Jellyfin version: the sign-in action was not recognised. Signing in with the user name is not affected.
cfg.help.emailLogin: If ticked, a user can type their confirmed e-mail address instead of their user name on the sign-in screen of any app. An address shared by several accounts cannot be used. After 3 failed sign-ins on the account (fewer if its lockout threshold is low), the address stops working until the user signs in with their user name. Mail Concierge does not limit or ban sign-in attempts: put fail2ban or an equivalent in front of Jellyfin.
